newsitem.title: CHINA: Most HK youths say they are "not Chinese" - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most HK youths say they are "not Chinese" - poll.

text.p: Over 50 per cent of Hong Kong's youth said they considered themselves Hong Kong people, not Chinese, a Hong Kong daily said on Sunday.

The result of a poll, conducted shortly before the British colony was handed back to China at midnight on June 30, showed that Hong Kong's young people had a deep sense of belonging to the territory, the Chinese-language newspaper Ming Pao said.
The poll was conducted by a voluntary group, the Hong Kong Playground Association, which surveyed about 200 people aged between 15 and 30.
While 55 percent of those polled said they considered themselves Hong Kongers, only 17.8 per cent regarded themselves as Chinese, according to the poll.
While 1.5 per cent were extremely happy at the prospect of the Chinese national flag flying high in Hong Kong, 13.2 per cent said they hated it.
Over 90 per cent of the territory's 6.4 million population are ethnic Chinese.
